episode_title: What Buyers Learn From How Fast You Close Your Books

real_qa.q: What is the acceptable timeline for closing monthly books in IT services firms preparing for acquisition?
real_qa.r: Timely management usually means within two weeks of the close of the month, which is generally accepted as a timely close. If it takes two months, there will be a lot of questions by buyers about the maturity of your financial systems and accounting governance. Even if it is multi-currency or multi-country, it should not be a markedly delayed process.
real_qa.requete: IT services close books timeline acquisition buyers

real_qa.q: What key performance metrics should IT services firms track and share with teams beyond headline P&L numbers?
real_qa.r: IT services companies should track utilization and realization as primary levers, with a target of 80% against a 2080-hour year for utilization. Beyond that, teams should understand recurring versus one-time revenue, how pricing and utilization impact gross margin per customer, and contractual arrangements that affect utilization. The business should also measure pipeline cleanliness every two weeks and review results against budgeted goals on a monthly basis with key team members.
real_qa.requete: IT services utilization realization metrics team transparency

guest.bio_context: Mike is a financial strategy expert at Revenue Rocket who advises tech-enabled services firms on accounting policies, financial governance, and CFO-level decision making. He advocates for transparent financial reporting and has experience helping business owners transition away from being the sole keeper of financial information in their companies.

real_quote: It lubricates the business operations to have that transparency. It gives people more responsibility as they're working within their lane in the business.
key_stats: Two weeks: accepted timeline for closing monthly books
80% utilization target against a 2080-hour year for IT services staff
$5 million to $50 million: revenue range for firms transitioning from cash-based to accrual-based accounting
$3 million to $5 million: threshold where organizations should begin moving toward GAAP-based accounting
Biweekly cadence for reviewing utilization levers and pipeline cleanliness
Monthly reporting cadence for key team members (sales, delivery leaders) with full financial results
